intro: To open preferences in Slack on a Mac, press ⌘ , (Command and comma) while the Slack desktop app is in front. You can also click your profile picture in the sidebar and choose Preferences.

blocks.text: Slack puts your personal settings in one window called Preferences. On a Mac, you can reach it in two common ways. One is a keyboard shortcut. The other is a menu that starts at your profile picture. Both lead to the same window, and this page covers each route, plus the fixes you need when something goes wrong.
Open preferences with the keyboard shortcut

Make Slack the active app first. Click an empty part of the Slack window, or switch to Slack with your usual app switcher. Then hold Command, tap the comma key, and let go. The shortcut is written ⌘ , in this guide, and Preferences opens in its own window.

Slack's screen reader help article gives the same shortcut for Mac. It says to press Command plus Comma to open your preferences. On Windows and Linux, the shortcut uses Ctrl plus Comma instead. That detail matters if you switch between a Mac and another computer.

The comma key sits near the M key on a standard US keyboard, on the bottom row. Other keyboard layouts can put it somewhere else. Apple says shortcuts can differ by language and keyboard layout, so the key you press may not match the guide exactly.

Slack's help center documents this shortcut for the desktop app only. If you use Slack in a browser, do not count on ⌘ , working there. Use the profile picture route instead, because Slack's help center describes that route for both versions.
Open preferences from your profile picture

If you prefer the mouse or trackpad, start in the left sidebar. Click your profile picture. Choose Preferences from the menu that opens. Slack's notifications help article gives this same path for the desktop app on Windows, Mac, and Linux.

Click the picture itself. Clicking a channel or a message does not lead to Preferences in the steps Slack documents. If you see a menu without Preferences in it, close the menu and try again on your picture.
What you will find inside Preferences

Preferences is split into tabs. Slack's help articles name Notifications and Advanced. They also mention an Accessibility tab, which is worth a look if you use assistive tools. Notifications controls when Slack alerts you. Advanced holds search options.

Tabs can change over time. Slack's update log says sidebar tabs were consolidated in September 2025 and can be reordered in September 2026. Those changes were made to the sidebar, not to Preferences, so the tab names in this guide should still help you find your way.
Change notification settings in Preferences

Say a busy channel keeps sending alerts you do not need. Open Preferences, then click Notifications. Slack's notifications article documents this route for the desktop app. Change one setting at a time, then watch how alerts behave over the next day.
Write down what you changed. If you change several things at once, you cannot tell which change helped. This habit takes a minute and saves you from undoing good settings later.
Limit search results by excluding channels

Search can fill with results from a noisy channel. Slack's search article describes the fix. Open your profile picture, choose Preferences, select Advanced, then find Search options. Add the channels you want to exclude from results.

The same article says these steps work from the desktop app or from Slack in your browser. In a browser, the Advanced area also has a setting where Cmd F or Ctrl F starts a Slack search. Check that setting if the shortcut does nothing for you in a browser.

For a quick test, run a search you ran last week. Compare the results before and after you exclude a channel. If the channel no longer appears, the setting worked. If you want the full search workflow, read [how to search messages in Slack on Mac](/how-to/search-messages-in-slack).

blocks.text: Check your Slack version before you troubleshoot

Menu labels and shortcuts can change between builds. Slack's Mac release notes list 4.53.280 as the latest stable build with a date you can verify, Nov 3, 2026. That release note covers security improvements.

The recent Mac release notes do not mention menus, Preferences, settings, or navigation. That is useful, but it does not guarantee your screen matches this guide. Follow the labels you see, and treat this page as a map rather than a script.
When the shortcut does not open Preferences

Start by making sure Slack is the active app. Then check the menu bar. Apple's help says that if a shortcut does not work, you should look in the app menus for the correct one, because shortcuts can differ by language and keyboard layout.

Next, look for a conflict. Open System Settings, go to Keyboard, then Keyboard Shortcuts. Apple says a warning icon appears next to conflicting shortcuts. Double-click the shortcut and press the new key combination to change it.

Last, fully quit Slack with ⌘ Q and open it again. This tip comes from community guides, not from Slack's help center, so treat it as a test rather than an official fix. Some utilities also grab key combinations. If one is running, quit it and try the shortcut again.

Here is a worked example. You press ⌘ , in Slack and nothing happens. You click the Slack window and try again, with the same result. You open System Settings, check Keyboard Shortcuts, and find a warning icon next to a conflict. You change that shortcut, and Preferences opens when you press ⌘ , again.
When your IT team locks a setting

On a work Mac, an administrator may control some defaults. Slack's configuration article says desktop app configuration is supported for version 4.31 and higher. Admins use .plist or .mobileconfig files under the domain com.tinyspeck.slackmacgap.
If a setting will not change, do not keep guessing. Ask your admin whether that setting is managed. That answer usually saves more time than any shortcut fix.
Use Preferences in Slack in a browser

Slack in a browser has the same profile picture route. Slack's search article says those steps work from the desktop app or from Slack in your browser. The ⌘ , shortcut is not documented for the browser, so start from the profile picture there.

The browser setting that makes Cmd F or Ctrl F start a Slack search lives under the same Preferences path. If you use both the desktop app and a browser, check that setting in each place and note which one you changed.
Common mistakes with Preferences in Slack

items: Clicking the wrong spot. Use your profile picture in the sidebar, not a channel name.
Pressing ⌘ , while another app is in front. Click the Slack window first.
Following an old screenshot. Tab names can change, so match the labels on your screen.
Assuming the shortcut works in a browser. Slack documents it only for the desktop app.
Skipping the conflict check. A conflicting shortcut can stop the keys from working, so check before you decide Slack is broken.

blocks.text: What to do after Preferences opens

Change one setting at a time. Close Preferences when you finish. Reopen it later with the same route to confirm the change held. A setting that looks wrong in the moment often works fine once you see it in use.

If your next job is clearing unread items, read [how to mark all messages as read in Slack on Mac](/how-to/mark-all-messages-as-read-in-slack). It covers the Unreads view and the steps that follow it.

Slack's labels can change, so trust the screen in front of you over any guide, including this one. Remember the two routes, the shortcut and the profile picture, and you can get to Preferences from almost any state of the app.

faq.question: What is the keyboard shortcut for Preferences in Slack on Mac?
faq.answer: The shortcut is Command and comma, written ⌘ ,. Slack's screen reader help article documents it for Mac. Make sure the Slack desktop app is in front before you press it.

faq.question: Does the shortcut work in Slack in a browser?
faq.answer: Slack documents ⌘ , only for the desktop app. In a browser, use the profile picture route instead. Slack's search article says those steps work from either the desktop app or Slack in your browser.

faq.question: Where is Preferences if the shortcut does nothing?
faq.answer: Click your profile picture in the sidebar, then choose Preferences. If the shortcut still fails, check the menu bar for the correct shortcut and look for a conflict in System Settings under Keyboard Shortcuts.

faq.question: How do I change notification settings in Slack on Mac?
faq.answer: Open Preferences, then click Notifications. Slack's notifications article uses this path for the desktop app on Windows, Mac, and Linux. Change one setting at a time so you can see what each change does.

faq.question: Why can I not change a setting in Preferences?
faq.answer: Your IT team may manage that setting through a configuration file. Slack's configuration article covers desktop app version 4.31 and higher. Contact your admin if a setting is locked on your Mac.

faq.question: Which Slack version should I use for these steps?
faq.answer: Slack's Mac release notes list 4.53.280 as the latest stable build with a verifiable date, Nov 3, 2026. Those notes do not mention changes to menus or Preferences. Follow the labels on your screen if they differ from this guide.

faq.question: Can I hide one channel from search results in Slack?
faq.answer: Yes. Open Preferences, choose Advanced, find Search options, and add the channel to the exclude list. Slack's search article describes this path. Test with a search you ran before to confirm the result.

faq.question: Does Slack's help center name the Slack menu bar item for Preferences?
faq.answer: No. Slack's help articles name the profile picture route and the ⌘ , shortcut. They do not name the menu bar item, so check the menu bar yourself if you want to confirm the exact label.

steps.name: Bring Slack to the front
steps.text: Click the Slack window, or switch to Slack with your usual app switcher. The shortcut only works for the app that is active, so this step matters.
steps.tip: If nothing opens, the active app is probably not Slack.

steps.name: Press Command and comma
steps.text: Hold Command, tap the comma key, and let go. Preferences opens in its own window. Slack's screen reader help article gives this same shortcut for Mac.
steps.tip: On a standard US keyboard, the comma key sits near the M key. Other layouts put it elsewhere.

steps.name: Or start from your profile picture
steps.text: Click your profile picture in the left sidebar, then choose Preferences from the menu. Slack's notifications help article uses this exact path for the desktop app.

steps.name: Pick the tab you need
steps.text: Preferences is split into tabs. Slack's help articles name Notifications, Advanced, and Accessibility. Click a tab in the window to switch to it.

steps.name: Open Notifications
steps.text: Select Notifications to control when Slack alerts you. Change one setting at a time so you can see what each change does.

steps.name: Open Advanced for search options
steps.text: Select Advanced. Search options live in this tab, and they let you exclude channels from search results.

steps.name: Add channels to exclude
steps.text: Under Search options, add the channels you do not want in search results. Then close the window and run a search to confirm the channel no longer appears.

steps.name: Use the browser route in a browser
steps.text: In Slack in a browser, use the same profile picture route. The ⌘ , shortcut is documented only for the desktop app, so do not rely on it in a browser.
steps.tip: Use the browser setting that makes Cmd F or Ctrl F start a search only if you want that behavior.

steps.name: Close Preferences
steps.text: Close the Preferences window when you finish. You can reopen it any time with the shortcut or the profile picture route.

troubleshooting.problem: Shortcut still fails after you check the menu
troubleshooting.fix: Fully quit Slack with ⌘ Q, then open it again. This tip comes from community guides, not Slack's help center, so treat it as a test. Quit any utility that grabs key combinations.

troubleshooting.problem: A setting is locked or will not change
troubleshooting.fix: Your administrator may manage it. Slack's configuration article covers desktop app version 4.31 and higher, using .plist or .mobileconfig files under com.tinyspeck.slackmacgap. Ask your admin before you try workarounds.

troubleshooting.problem: Tabs look different from this guide
troubleshooting.fix: Slack changes its interface over time. Its update log describes sidebar tab changes in September 2025 and September 2026. Follow the tab names on your screen rather than their position.

troubleshooting.problem: The profile picture menu has no Preferences entry
troubleshooting.fix: Click the profile picture itself, not a channel or a message, and try again. If Preferences is still missing, compare your build with the latest stable Mac build, 4.53.280, in Slack's release notes.
